name: Nuclear plant safety
value: ZNPP worker killed 9 Nov; power cut 8 Nov
summary: A Zaporizhzhia plant worker was killed by a drone on 9 Nov, a day after off-site power was lost; no safety-system damage
state: Zaporizhzhia lost its off-site power on 8 Nov when the Ferosplavna line disconnected and relied on diesel generators to cool its reactors; the IAEA said the cause was not yet known (The Edge Malaysia). On 9 Nov a plant worker was killed in a drone attack, the second in under two weeks, and IAEA Director General Grossi said such attacks breach basic nuclear safety principles (United24 Media). Searches on 16 Nov found no damage to safety-critical systems, INES level 2 event or radiological release.
for_you: There is no radiological risk to the UK. People in Ukraine should follow national civil protection guidance; UK travellers should check FCDO travel advice.
rubric_hit: Watch: plant lost all off-site power 8 Nov and drone strike killed worker 9 Nov; no safety-system damage

why: Fighting near nuclear power plants risks a radiological release; the IAEA reports on Zaporizhzhia and other plants in or near war zones.
drivers: Off-site power losses, strikes near plants, staffing, cooling water, military occupation.

rubric.alert: Damage to safety-critical systems, an INES level 2 or higher event, or a radiological release.
rubric.watch: A plant loses all off-site power, strikes land near a plant, or the IAEA reports a deteriorating safety situation.
rubric.normal: No new IAEA safety concerns at plants in or near conflict zones.
